final.memo:
Charlie and I view the current market climate as one of those rare times when stocks in general are undeniably cheap. With the market having fallen over 40% from its peak and earnings yields sitting significantly above bond yields, we are being presented with the kind of value that does not require us to forecast macro-economic turns or guess at the path of the index. Our approach remains anchored in finding understandable businesses—those with durable moats and pricing power—that we can buy at a significant margin of safety [D01, D04].

While the headlines are dominated by fears of depression, inflation, and resource scarcity, these are precisely the times when a patient investor can build wealth by focusing on the underlying economics of individual businesses rather than the mood of the market [D03, D05]. We have no interest in predicting whether the current rebound will hold or if the bottom is truly in; we simply know that when the price of a dollar of earnings is this low relative to alternative safe investments, our duty is to be aggressive buyers of wonderful businesses at fair prices [D01, D03].
